title: Audit checkpoints are not signed or anchored outside the primary database

original_titles.title: No external signed audit checkpoints despite docstring claim

problem: audit.py implements an in-database hash chain but no periodic signed checkpoint export to independent storage. A database administrator who can rewrite all rows can recompute the chain.
impact: The chain is tamper-evident only while the primary database itself remains trusted. A full DB compromise can rewrite evidence without an external anchor.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Create a scheduled checkpoint job that reads each chain head and signs scope, seq, hash, timestamp and schema/version with a private key held outside the database.
Write checkpoints to a separate account/bucket with append-only/object-lock retention and separate credentials. Do not store the signing private key in the DB or the same host.
Record checkpoint id, signature, storage URI and verification outcome. Alert when the expected checkpoint interval is exceeded.
Add a verifier that downloads the last checkpoint, verifies signature and compares the live chain prefix. Include restore drill validation.
Correct the audit module docstring until the external checkpoint process is implemented and observed in production.

acceptance_criteria: A database-only administrator cannot forge a valid external checkpoint.
A tampered chain prefix fails external verification.
Missing checkpoint intervals trigger an alert.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
